title: DeSlopify your game: Animations are the most obvious visuals that scream slop, and I'm using paid assets to fix that
author: Ok-Pirate5732
selftext:
As many of us have quickly found out, animations are by far where AI tools lag behind the most, and therefore are one of the most obvious signalers of "slop". Thus far, I've been relying on free animation libraries, but these are limited.

 I've spent a lot of time trying to make a cohesive art style/direction, and in isolation my developer tunnel vision had me believing my attempts to edit some animations into attacks for other weapon types were "passable", even if I knew they weren't up to par with the rest of the art. They clearly were way worse lol

I went ahead and got licenses to professional animation assets, and while there is still a bit of tweaking I need to do, I think they make a huge difference to the overall polish of the game. A friendly reminder for myself and anyone else making a full game for the first time with AI that what looks a little like slop to yourself can look really sloppy to anyone that hasn't spent hours looking at your game. Take advantage of other tools out there. 

Please let me know what you think it made a difference or if I wasted my money lol 

\--

*If you're curious, the game is* [*100 Bodies in the Grass*](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5357660/100_Bodies_in_the_Grass/)

Other markers I've seen playing games that felt like slop:

* The gameplay loop revealed everything in the first 5 minutes
* It doesn't stay fun past the first hour
* There's a pixelated/old tv filter
* It uses 2d assets in a 3d world
* The progression is just numbers: more damage, more hp, more speed, more monsters
* It's not a game, it's a simulator

replies.author: fukinrage85
replies.body: I hear you. I agree there is some true slop out there.  Likely poor concepts if they aren't fun, or the dev(s) are just being impatient or lazy in the dev process. Quality games take years. 2D assets are easier to generate with AI so there's less of a barrier to entry. Novel ideas or mechanics are hard and requires out of the box thinking... like, how many cozy fishing games do we need? If you genuinely move the needle forward for novelty or mechanics, then sure, but just copying released games with a different skin (sometimes far worse than the original) is just poor taste. Don't release a game on Steam if it's a re-skin of something else. Learning is learning but not all learning is sellable.
